audit.whatIsWrong: Level chart gave Viktor 6 of 7 stages while Aurelion Sol wins the matchup 52.88% over 1477 games, and the full layer (phases[4..6].side = Skill) already disagreed with the content layer (win[4..6] = Viktor/Viktor/Aurelion Sol).
audit.why: Viktor genuinely owns levels 1-5 (Gravity Field is the only reliable cancel on Breath of Light's channel), but Falling Star at 6 evens it and Aurelion Sol's permanent Stardust curve passes a Viktor who plateaus after his last augment.
audit.corrected: Viktor / Viktor / Viktor / Viktor / Skill / Aurelion Sol / Aurelion Sol, proposed as matched full+content pairs.

audit.whatIsWrong: Spikes referenced 'Chaos Storm', 'Death Ray' and 'Comet of Legend' — none of which exist.
audit.why: Viktor's R is Arcane Storm and his E is Hextech Ray; Aurelion Sol has no ability called Comet of Legend, his scaling resource is Stardust and his R is Falling Star / The Skies Descend.
audit.corrected: Spikes rewritten around Arcane Storm (120/100/80s), Hextech Ray (12/11/10/9/8s), Hex Fragment augments, Rod of Ages and the Stardust curve.

audit.whatIsWrong: The decisive channel interaction was never stated in either direction.
audit.why: Both Breath of Light (Q) and Astral Flight (W) are interruptible channels and Gravity Field's stun is the only thing in Viktor's kit that cancels them. Conversely Arcane Storm is itself a channel, so Falling Star's stun cancels it outright. Siphon Power also grants a shield, so chip trades fund his augments rather than threatening him.
audit.corrected: Stated in early, mid, breakdown.cooldowns, whys[1], whys[4] and spikes[1].

audit.why: Concrete numbers make the advice actionable.
audit.corrected: Gravity Field 17/16/15/14/13s, Hextech Ray 12s rank 1, Arcane Storm 120s rank 1 now appear in breakdown.cooldowns, early and ahead.

edits.before: His Siphon Power farm denial keeps you off CS and behind on stacks
edits.after: Siphon Power shields his trades and keeps you off CS and off stacks

edits.before: Chaos Storm at 6 gives him a decisive damage and zoning advantage over your Comet of Legend
edits.after: Arcane Storm at 6 zones you, but your Falling Star stun cancels its channel outright

edits.before: Even with your first item his scaling keeps him ahead in raw damage output
edits.after: Rod of Ages plus banked Stardust tip the E-execute waveclear war your way

edits.before: Chaos Storm gives him a massive teamfight and lane-bully tool that out-damages your Comet of Legend in a straight trade, since his storm follows and zones you out of safe positioning.
edits.after: Arcane Storm follows you and interrupts your Breath of Light channel, but it is a channel itself — your Falling Star stun ends it, and a 120-second ultimate spent on nothing is your window.

edits.before: Even through his first Hex Core upgrade Viktor's scaling stays strong, and his Death Ray/Siphon Power combo continues to out-poke your early-item power spike.
edits.after: Through his first Hex Fragment augment, Hextech Ray plus Siphon Power still out-pokes you, but Rod of Ages and E executes let you match his waveclear from safety.

edits.before: Once you're fully stacked with Comet of Legend and 2+ items your global threat and burst finally edge past his augmented abilities, since Viktor's damage plateaus after his final Hex Core while your stars keep compounding.
edits.after: Once you're deep into Stardust with 2+ items, Breath of Light burns through Siphon Power's shield faster than he can recast it, since Viktor's damage plateaus after his last augment while your stacks keep compounding permanently.

edits.before: Viktor's Siphon Power poke and Gravity Field zoning make it very hard to farm safely or find angles to stack your Q, and he snowballs his Hex Core upgrades off this early lane dominance while your kit is still ramping, so you're on the back foot through the laning phase.
edits.after: Gravity Field is 17 seconds at rank 1 and it is the only thing in his kit that cancels your Breath of Light channel, so bank stacks while it is down and give ground while it is up; Siphon Power shields him through chip damage, so never trade for a kill pre-6.

edits.before: Chaos Storm at 6 is a genuine problem — it out-damages an unstacked Comet of Legend in a straight fight and lets him zone you away from CS or force you off position entirely, and this power gap persists even as he starts building his first completed item.
edits.after: Arcane Storm at 6 zones you off CS and interrupts your channels, but it is a channel too — Falling Star cancels it outright, and a 120-second ultimate spent on nothing is your all-in window. That math holds right through his first completed item.

edits.before: It isn't until you're fully stacked with your own Comet of Legend online and two items banked that your global pick potential and stacked-star burst finally start to edge past his damage, since Viktor's power curve flattens after his last Hex Core while yours keeps climbing with every star.
edits.after: It isn't until you're fully stacked with your own Stardust curve online and two items banked that your global pick potential and stacked-star burst finally start to edge past his damage, since Viktor's power curve flattens after his last augment while yours keeps climbing with every star.

edits.before: - Viktor Gravity Field: matchup-defining — The stun zone owns every all-in — walk out the moment it drops or fight outside it. Read it like a second minimap. - Guard your W Astral Flight like a fifth summoner spell. - Ultimate goes to kill windows only.
edits.after: - Gravity Field: 17/16/15/14/13s and the only cancel on your Q channel — walk out the instant it drops, and start the beam the second it is spent. - Hextech Ray is 12s at rank 1: his poke window, not his kill window. - Arcane Storm is 120s at rank 1 — cancel it with R.

edits.before: Carry by scaling honestly — every stardust stack is permanent, and the 30-minute version of you wins fights your laning self cannot imagine.
edits.after: Carry by outliving his augments — Stardust never falls off, and once Breath of Light burns through Siphon Power's shield he stops mattering.

edits.before: Ahead, compound it: shove with E executes, burn Viktor on every W rotation, and group early — your beam turns small mid-game leads into unanswerable objective control.
edits.after: Ahead, take his farm: shove with E, then W over the wall and burn him off the side wave — Gravity Field on 13s cannot cover both, and he stalls out on augments.

edits.before: Viktor wins by landing Gravity Field, denying your pattern, and keeping the fight at a distance your kit resents.
edits.after: Viktor wins by stunning you inside Gravity Field mid-channel, then killing you before Astral Flight comes back up.

edits.before: The stun zone owns every all-in — walk out the moment it drops or fight outside it. Its cooldown is the green light — wait for it.
edits.after: Every second of beam on a champion is permanent Stardust — drag it across him while he walks to a wave, never while Gravity Field is up.

edits.before: That’s Viktor’s bread-and-butter play — deny it and they run out of answers.
edits.after: Siphon Power's shield eats your chip, so pre-item trades only fund his augments.

notes: Fabricated names killed: 'Chaos Storm' -> Arcane Storm, 'Death Ray' -> Hextech Ray, 'Comet of Legend' (does not exist on Aurelion Sol) -> Stardust / Falling Star. 'Hex Core' is legacy naming; the current passive grants Hex Fragments that augment abilities, so I moved to 'augment'. Level chart was self-contradictory across layers (phases[4..6].side=Skill vs win[4..6]=Viktor/Viktor/Aurelion Sol) — proposed as matched pairs. Left breakdown.wave and dosFull[2].d alone: already grounded in this enemy.
